headline: Isaias Comes Ashore Near Destin at 105 mph
deck: The Category 2 storm hit the U.S. Florida Panhandle at 8:30 p.m. Central Time on 9 October, then weakened over land.
body: Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the western Florida Panhandle on Friday, 9 October 2026, at 8:30 p.m. Central Time, near Destin, Florida. [E1][E3]
This paper's 9 October file had the hurricane expected to make landfall late Friday or early Saturday between the Mississippi coast and the western Florida panhandle. [E9]
Maximum sustained winds were 105 mph, making it a Category 2 hurricane, and the minimum central pressure was 971 millibars. [E2]
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis told ABC that wind shear weakened the storm from a Category 3 to a Category 2 before landfall, although strong winds and heavy rainfall remained significant threats. [E5]
Hurricane Isaias continued north over the western Florida Panhandle on Friday night, although it weakened to a Category 1 storm. [E4]
The Florida National Guard has activated 13 route clearance teams to immediately respond following landfall. [E6]
Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport closed to commercial service. [E7]
More than 60 bridge inspectors are staged to deploy and begin bridge inspections immediately following severe weather. [E8]
